anomaly_def.Name: Data Block and Index Integrity Anomaly + Storage Space Capacity Anomaly + Network and Connectivity Resource Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Data Block and Index Integrity Anomaly : Persisted data- or index-page contents, linkages, or checksums are damaged so that on-disk structures no longer faithfully represent the logical rows and keys.
Storage Space Capacity Anomaly : The database, log, temporary, or backup storage reaches hard capacity limits, preventing further allocation or auto-extension operations.
Network and Connectivity Resource Anomaly : Listener, socket, or network-path resources are exhausted or unstable, limiting the rate at which clients can establish sessions or transfer result sets.

When the three root causes act at the same time, symptoms overlap and reinforce each other: 1) corrupted indexes force query plans to abandon selective access paths and fall back to heap scans or full index rebuild attempts; 2) those heavier scans and emergency rebuilds explode data-file growth, temporary-segment usage, and redo/undo volume, rapidly consuming the remaining storage headroom; 3) as space depletion triggers allocation failures, affected statements hang in space-wait states, and log archival or checkpoint progress stalls, cascading more sessions into backlog; 4) the increasing execution latency, coupled with connection-slot exhaustion and retransmissions caused by the network anomaly, produces a spike of connection timeouts, half-open sockets, and client retries; 5) monitoring shows an apparently erratic mixture of corruption errors, out-of-space errors, and connection refusals that are difficult to attribute to a single layer.

Causally, page or index corruption can initiate large-scale table scans, online repairs, or forced rebuilds that accelerate space consumption. The resulting space scarcity, in turn, amplifies the corruption impact because failed allocations abort in-place rebuilds and leave structures only partially repaired, deepening logical inconsistency. Both the corruption-induced long-running operations and the space-related stalls hold server back-end processes longer, inflating concurrent session counts. The saturated connection layer then drops or throttles new sessions, causing clients to retry and pile additional load on an already resource-starved and logically inconsistent engine. Each anomaly thus feeds the others: corruption drives space growth, space limits stall recovery and normal processing, and network saturation hides or delays error feedback while multiplying connection pressure, jointly degrading availability and increasing the risk of further corruption through incomplete I/O or abort sequences.

entry.official_description: Cannot use %s as an undo tablespace because it does not end with '.ibu'.
entry.cause_analysis: The failure is typically associated with file creation, filesystem access, write durability, log persistence, tablespace management, or storage-capacity boundaries.
entry.solution_guidance: Inspect filesystem capacity and permissions, verify persistence paths, review log and data placement, and check whether storage latency or write failures are affecting the engine.
